jurisdiction.handoffText: The package goes to the offices of your U.S. representative and both of your state's senators. They decide whether to introduce it. The public record stays open either way.

issue.name: Invasive species
issue.title: Invasive species and the federal government
facts: USDA's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) keeps foreign pests and diseases out and works with states on eradication.
The Plant Protection Act (2000) covers plant pests; the Lacey Act bans listed injurious animals; Executive Order 13112 (1999) created the National Invasive Species Council.
Congress enacted $1.16 billion for APHIS for fiscal year 2026.
Customs and Border Protection's own staffing model calls for 721 more agriculture specialists at ports of entry.
lists: Federal agencies reported spending about $2.3 billion on invasive species in FY2016
Selected invasive species cost the U.S. economy an estimated $127 billion a year
Islands and territories like Hawaiʻi face the highest risk of new arrivals
Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry
Funding passes through the House and Senate Appropriations subcommittees on Agriculture
sources: CRS, invasive species laws and agencies
groups: Leans toward border enforcement and protecting farmers, wary of new costs on business.
Leans toward steady funding for states, research, and having importers share the cost.

statements.text: Hire the extra agriculture specialists that Customs and Border Protection says it needs at ports of entry.
States and territories should get steady federal grants for rapid response to new pests.
APHIS should publish a public national map of confirmed pest detections.
Penalties for knowingly importing banned species should go up.
Invasive species work should have a dedicated trust fund instead of depending on yearly appropriations.
Fund more research on biological controls, like natural predators of pests.
Importers and shippers should pay more of the cost of inspections.
Farmers hit by federal pest quarantines should get prompt compensation.
Islands and territories should get extra federal help because they face the highest risk.

revenue.name: Raise penalties for importing banned species
revenue.note: Penalties mainly deter. The revenue estimate is rough.
revenue.billText: The maximum civil and criminal penalties for knowingly importing an injurious species or a prohibited plant pest are increased.

revenue.name: Importer fee revenue not yet estimated
revenue.note: Would bring in money rather than cost it, but the amount depends on fee design and import volumes. Analysts would estimate it before it could be counted.
